title: Shehnai
summary: The shehnai is a double-reed wind instrument of north India, played at celebrations and in classical recitals. A pair of reeds sits in a conical wooden tube with finger holes and a flared brass bell. Its voice is sweet, a little nasal, and the player bends gently between the notes.
howToPlay: A covered hole glows; an open hole shows its dark bore. Six notes of the mode are lit down the tube.
Each strike shows the fingering of that note and the bell opens as it sounds.
Long notes swell slowly: strike close to the beat and let them ring.
rules: A phrase is a line of notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The shehnai is heard at weddings and festivals across north India, and in concert halls, where a drone sounds underneath the melody.
